prompt: What does HTTP status code 418 mean?

messages.content: You are a helpful assistant with access to tools. When you need information from the workspace, or need to run a command, call the appropriate tool. Once you have enough information to answer, reply directly with the answer in plain text and do NOT call any more tools.
What does HTTP status code 418 mean?

events.reply:
HTTP status code 418 means "I'm a teapot."

It originated from an April Fools' joke RFC published in 1998 (RFC 2324, the "Hyper Text Coffee Pot Control Protocol"). The idea is that a teapot, when asked to brew coffee, should refuse and return this error because it is, in fact, a teapot and not a coffee pot. RFC 7168 later extended it to the "Hyper Text Coffee Pot Control Protocol for Tea Efflux Appliances."

Although it was never intended as a serious part of the HTTP standard, 418 became a well-known in-joke among developers. Many web frameworks and libraries implement it as an Easter egg, and some real-world services use it humorously to indicate that a request has been refused (for example, to signal automated/bot traffic that is being blocked).

In 2017 there was a brief effort to remove 418 from some codebases (notably a proposal in Node.js and Python), which prompted a community campaign ("Save 418") to preserve it. The IANA HTTP status code registry now formally reserves 418 as "Unused," with a note that it was defined in the teapot RFCs, specifically to prevent it from being reassigned to a serious purpose.
